parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by the de Broglie wavelength.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of an electron moving at a speed of $4.9 \times 10^7 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: State **one** similarity and **one** difference between an electron and a positron.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: An electron moving at a speed of $4.9 \times 10^7 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ collides with a positron that is travelling at the same speed in the opposite direction. As a result of the collision, two gamma-ray photons are produced.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: State the name of this type of reaction.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: State what happens to the electron and to the positron.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why two gamma-ray photons are produced, rather than just one.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text: Show that the kinetic energy of the electron before the collision is $1.1 \times 10^{-15} \text{ J}$.

parts.label: (d)(v)
parts.text: Use the information in **(d)(iv)** to determine, to three significant figures, the wavelength associated with the gamma radiation emitted in the collision.
